Sand says public safety officials should be first heard on property tax law effects

By Isabella Warren
Published: Sep. 15, 2026 at 6:43 PM EDT|Updated: 8 hours ago
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:53
Instaread

DES MOINES, Iowa (Gray Media Iowa State Capitol Bureau) — Democratic gubernatorial candidate Rob Sand said Iowa’s public safety officials should come first for decision making, as cities warn they will need to make cuts to first responders under a new property tax reform law.

Sand said supporting law enforcement is more than giving them a seat at the table. With cities including Des Moines cutting public safety positions amid budget pressures, Sand said he will watch how the state’s new property tax law affects departments and listen to law enforcement if they say it is making things harder.

“When you listen to people who are making sacrifices, who are putting their lives on the line, and they have legitimate complaints you would think that your first reaction would be to let’s get these people what they need because they’ve given a lot for us,” Sand said.

Des Moines budget cuts

Public safety in Iowa is facing shortfalls and cuts in some cities. This week, the city of Des Moines approved $11 million in budget cuts, including nearly $1 million in reductions to public safety positions.

The Des Moines City Council pointed to recently passed property tax reform, which caps revenue at 2%, for the cuts.

Sand said he is keeping watch on the issue in the months ahead.

“As much as people have confidence and what’s going to happen the truth is that we are only months into a brand new property tax regime in the state of Iowa and we need to have some experience with it before we start making changes about what the issues are,” Sand said.

Earlier this year, Indianola Mayor Steve Richardson said the city cut seven positions last year, including four in the police department, and said more reductions could come as a result of the property tax reform.

Republican opponent responds

Sand’s Republican opponent, Zach Lahn’s campaign said in a statement that Sand “thinks Iowans have to choose between safe communities and affordable property taxes.” Lahn’s campaign said if elected, Lahn will expand the tax base so more people are contributing, rather than constantly demanding more from the same taxpayers.

Sand said first responders will be the first people he listens to when it comes to any property tax changes.

“If we’re hearing from them something consistently that’s the first place where we should be willing to listen to that and make changes based on what we’re hearing back,” Sand said.

Endorsements and cancer coverage law

Sand has said one of his “day one” priorities if elected is public safety. He announced endorsements from 60 firefighters, police, sheriffs and others, and said his plan is to do more to protect those who work in public safety.

Iowa firefighters have fought for years to expand their health insurance benefits. In 2025, Gov. Kim Reynolds signed into law legislation that expanded coverage for first responders diagnosed with cancer. Sand criticized how long it took leaders to pass that legislation and said when public safety officials have an issue, he will address it quickly if elected.

“The least that we can be doing is making sure that the exposure that they have to risk is something that we recognize, respect, and cover. Because the bottom line is they’re still going to be taking risks, they’re still risking life and limb on our behalf,” Sand said.

Lahn’s campaign said in a statement that police and firefighters are core functions of government and should be funded accordingly. The campaign said if elected, Lahn will “protect taxpayers, prioritize public safety and focus relentlessly on growing Iowa.”

---

Isabella Warren covers state government and politics for Gray Media-owned stations in Iowa. Email her at isabella.warren@kcrg.com; and follow her on Facebook at Isabella Warren TV on X/Twitter@isabellaw_gray, and on Instagram@IsabellaWarrenTV.
